official.description_text:
Postdoc in Large Language Model inferencing
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
The advertised post-doctoral position is within an ambitious, 5-year Wallenberg Scholar project titled "Scalable and adaptive inferencing for democratizing AI". In this 18 Million SEK project, we want to dramatically reduce the cost and power for serving large language models such as ChatGPT.
More project information
and our
project page
with early publications.
The work will primarily entail design, implementation, and evaluation of distributed systems and networks for machine learning inference. Applying machine learning concepts, with the goal of devising agentic frameworks, will also be a part of the project.
As a member of the research lab, you will be involved in experimental systems work in collaboration with faculty members and several doctoral students at our research lab. You will contribute to scientific publications as well as to new grant applications.
The work will be in collaboration with Professor Dejan Kostic and Associate Professor Marco Chiesa.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
You should also have a solid background in distributed systems, networking, programming and operating systems, and very good knowledge of English in speech and writing as it is required in day to day work.
It is important that you have very good skills in critical thinking and very good knowledge of C++, Python, Linux, and some scripting language.
We are seeking a highly motivated candidate with a willingness to experiment and explore, with international publications in journals and top conferences.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Teaching abilities and awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality.
You are a good collaborator but can also work independently.
Experience with machine learning, GPU programming, or large-scale inference systems.
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.
A
position as a postdoctoral fellow
is a time-limited qualified appointment focusing mainly on research, intended as a first career step after a dissertation.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position in distributed systems and ML inference for large language models, focused on reducing cost and power of LLM serving. Work includes systems design, implementation, evaluation, and ML concepts for agentic frameworks.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic alignment. The position is pure systems engineering and ML inference optimization for language models. The researcher's themes are human-centred XR, collaborative learning, spatial cognition, and immersive systems. LLM inferencing and cost optimization are algorithmic and infrastructure concerns with no connection to user experience, learning outcomes, collaboration mechanics, or spatial understanding. Mentions of 'agentic frameworks' are technical ML constructs, not agent-based social simulation or multiplayer interaction design.

methodological_fit.rationale: Minimal methodological fit. Position requires systems thinking (distributed systems, networking, operating systems), implementation skills (C++, Python, Linux), and experimental systems work. Researcher has intermediate multiplayer networking (Photon, Spatial.io) and advanced C# but no background in low-level systems, GPU programming, or distributed inference. The 'experimental' framing is fundamentally different—here it means building and benchmarking distributed systems; for researcher, it means user studies and spatial transfer evaluation.

growth_value.rationale: Moderate growth value in systems and infrastructure skills. Position would develop competence in distributed systems, networking, low-level systems programming (C++, Linux), and potentially GPU optimization—all valuable for scaling multiplayer XR backends. However, the focus on LLM inference is narrow and not directly applicable to immersive systems. Researcher would gain systems thinking and implementation depth but at opportunity cost of staying closer to HCI/XR domain.

strategic_value.rationale: Limited strategic value for target identity. Position is at KTH (target geography) with substantial funding (Wallenberg Scholar, 18M SEK) and strong publication expectations. However, the research group (distributed systems for ML inference) is orthogonal to human-centred immersive systems. Supervisors (Kostic, Chiesa) are systems researchers with no HCI or XR background. The postdoc label is standard, but the research trajectory diverges significantly from target identity. Funding stability and academic prestige do not offset domain mismatch.

eligibility_flags: Requires PhD in a relevant field or equivalence; researcher has MSc by Research in progress, not PhD—major eligibility blocker

Requires 'very good skills in critical thinking and very good knowledge of C++, Python, Linux, and some scripting language'; researcher has advanced C# but limited C++, beginner Python, no documented Linux or scripting experience

Requires 'international publications in journals and top conferences'; researcher has 1 first-author journal article and systematic mapping review in progress—below typical postdoc publication bar for this level of competition
'Experience with machine learning, GPU programming, or large-scale inference systems' is preferred; researcher has none
risks: PhD eligibility blocker; position requires PhD, researcher is MSc in progress
Publication record below typical KTH postdoc bar; likely to be competitive disadvantage even with eligible PhD
Systems depth mismatch; researcher's systems experience is at game engine/multiplayer networking level, not low-level distributed systems or GPU-level optimization
Career pivot; postdoc in LLM systems would further distance researcher from human-centred immersive systems trajectory
Supervisor group (distributed systems, ML inference) has no HCI, XR, or learning science expertise—poor mentorship fit
High-pressure environment (Wallenberg Scholar project, top-tier publication expectations) with domain mismatch creates risk of struggling and damaging early postdoc record
